stories.body: Wildfires driven by high winds and sustained heat have forced more than 300,000 people from homes or holiday areas in France and Spain. In southwestern France, flames moved inland toward Bordeaux, prompting evacuations across Gironde and Landes, the closure of Bordeaux airport and military support for firefighters. Spain declared a national emergency as major fires near Madrid and in Ávila threatened to merge; authorities warned residents to avoid outdoor activity because of smoke. A man was found dead in a car during a separate fire near Valencia, while emergency aircraft and ground crews from other European countries were deployed to help.
stories.headline: Wildfires force mass evacuations in France and Spain as blazes threaten Bordeaux and Madrid

stories.body: One person was killed and at least 16 others injured after a white van drove into people near Berlin's Christopher Street Day Pride celebrations in Tiergarten, close to the Brandenburg Gate. Police said the vehicle later crashed into a tree and was found abandoned, and a citywide manhunt is under way for 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. Germany's interior minister said the available evidence pointed to an Islamist terrorist attack, while investigators said details of the sequence of events and the suspect's precise role were still being established. The Pride event was cut short and some victims were reported to have life-threatening injuries.
stories.headline: Vehicle drives into Berlin Pride crowd, killing one and injuring at least 16

stories.body: Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned after weeks of youth-led protests over leaks in high-stakes entrance examinations, a major victory for the satirical Cockroach Janta Party movement. Pradhan said he respected young people's aspirations and resigned to prevent what he called anti-national forces from exploiting the unrest. The protests, which grew after a police crackdown on demonstrators marching toward parliament, channelled wider frustration over unemployment, corruption and government accountability. The movement called off its five-week protest after the resignation, saying the government had accepted its demands, including compensation for affected families and protections for protesters.
stories.headline: India's education minister resigns after youth-led 'Cockroach' protests over exam paper leaks

stories.body: Israeli forces arrested dozens of Palestinians in and around the West Bank village of Tal after a confrontation involving armed Israeli settlers, Palestinians and soldiers left four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers dead. Palestinian officials said settlers had approached the village to attack residents, while the Israeli military initially described the civilians as hikers before acknowledging that some were armed. Israel launched a broader military operation, raiding homes and detaining residents; Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu promised a forceful response, including measures against the family of a Palestinian involved and accelerated settlement approvals. Accounts of how the shooting began remain sharply disputed.
stories.headline: Israeli forces arrest dozens in West Bank village after deadly confrontation involving settlers

stories.body: UN Secretary-General António Guterres arrived in Damascus for the first visit to Syria by a serving UN chief since 2009, before the civil war that killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions. Guterres described the trip as a visit of solidarity and said Syria had an opportunity to build a more stable, inclusive and prosperous future after the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024. He is due to meet President Ahmed al-Sharaa, government officials and civil-society representatives, address the new parliament and visit UN peacekeepers in the south. He also said Israeli incursions into Syria were unacceptable and must stop.
stories.headline: UN chief António Guterres makes first visit to Syria by a serving secretary-general since before the civil war

stories.body: The death of a young soldier from Texas has prompted reflection in her hometown on the necessity and costs of the war with Iran, which has divided the country.
stories.headline: Texas community reflects on a soldier's death in Trump's Iran war

stories.body: A sprawling heat dome is bringing dangerous, persistent heat to much of the central United States, with roughly 80 million people under heat advisories from the Southwest and Gulf Coast through the Great Plains and Midwest. Forecasters warned that high humidity and unusually warm nights will limit recovery and allow heat stress to accumulate into the coming week. Temperatures in some areas are expected to run 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit above normal, with western Nebraska forecast to reach 108 degrees Fahrenheit.
stories.headline: Dangerous heat dome expands across the central United States

stories.body: The fatal police shooting of Corey Durell Ruiz, a homeless man who police say wounded an officer with a knife while resisting arrest, has roiled Madison, Wisconsin. Protesters have gathered and held a candlelight vigil, while community groups and Ruiz's family have called for accountability and action against racial injustice. Family lawyer Ben Crump said he believes the officer who fired the shots should face criminal charges.
stories.headline: Madison police shooting prompts protests and demands for accountability

stories.body: Spain expanded its national emergency response as major wildfires continued around Madrid, Ávila and Toledo, with officials warning that difficult weather conditions were hampering containment. More than 91,900 people had been evacuated or confined in Madrid and Ávila, and the fires had burned tens of thousands of hectares. Authorities urged residents to follow evacuation or confinement orders, while international assistance arrived from Portugal, Greece and Italy, including ground crews, vehicles and water-bombing aircraft. A separate fire near Vall d'Uixò in Castellón also forced the evacuation of about 15,000 people.
stories.headline: Spain expands national emergency response as major wildfires continue across Madrid, Ávila and Toledo

stories.body: Spain's Supreme Court has applied the amnesty law for the first time, ending potential criminal liability for eight people convicted of disobedience or public-order offenses connected to the Catalan independence movement. Those granted amnesty include four former members of the Catalan parliament's governing bureau, former Sabadell mayor Maties Serracant and three other citizens convicted over protests after the 2019 independence trial verdict. The decision follows a ruling by the Court of Justice of the European Union finding that the amnesty law did not conflict with EU legislation, while Spain's Constitutional Court has also rejected the final pending constitutional challenge to the measure.
stories.headline: Spain's Supreme Court applies the amnesty law for the first time to eight people convicted over Catalan independence-related offenses

stories.body: Plus Ultra president Julio Martínez Sola and chief executive Roberto Roselli have resigned while remaining under investigation over the airline's pandemic-era public bailout. The executives were summoned to testify after submitting court filings that acknowledged a contract providing for payments equivalent to 1% of the 53 million euro rescue package for assistance securing the aid. They said payments totaling about 530,000 euros were made through companies linked to a consultant, while the inquiry examines the circumstances surrounding the state loan. Minority shareholder Hugo Castaño is proposed to take over as executive president, subject to approval by the state industrial holding company SEPI.
stories.headline: Plus Ultra's president and CEO resign amid investigation into the airline's government bailout

stories.body: Rail infrastructure manager Adif has completed work to stabilize ground affected by a sinkhole at the Vallbona rail-undergrounding works and has authorized test runs for the suspended R2 and R11 commuter lines. The empty test trains will determine whether passengers can return safely, with Catalonia's transport minister, Sílvia Paneque, saying the monitoring data were encouraging and service could resume next week. Passengers using replacement buses have reported long waits, delays and uneven information. The R3 line remains suspended because of a separate rail-traffic-control problem, with no restoration timetable announced.
stories.headline: Adif begins safety testing to restore R2 and R11 commuter rail service after Vallbona sinkhole

stories.body: Residents displaced after a sinkhole at Barcelona's L9 metro construction works have formed a platform and hired a lawyer to seek compensation from the Catalan government for material, financial and emotional harm. They want a common framework agreement covering current and potentially affected residents, including people who report vibrations or new cracks in nearby buildings. Authorities say more residents will be allowed to return in the next two weeks, bringing the share of evacuated homes reopened to about 60%, while emergency payments of 1,200 euros a month, rising to as much as 2,000 euros depending on household circumstances, are due to begin next week.
stories.headline: Residents affected by Barcelona's L9 sinkhole prepare compensation claim against the Catalan government

stories.body: Catalonia's Civil Protection agency has activated the Inuncat flood alert for intense thunderstorms that could bring more than 20 litres of rain per square metre in 30 minutes, along with hail in some areas. The greatest risk initially lies in the northeastern counties of Garrotxa and Selva, though showers may affect the wider northeast as well as the central and southern coast overnight. Authorities urged people to monitor forecasts, avoid risky activities and never attempt to cross rivers, streams or ravines, where water levels can rise suddenly. Heavy rain has already forced the closure of the Sant Miquel del Fai natural area because of falling-rock risk.
stories.headline: Catalonia activates flood alert as intense rain and storms are forecast

stories.body: Barcelona's city council has approved proposals to examine subsidies and other measures to protect households most exposed to extreme heat. One plan calls for rapid aid for vulnerable homes to install temperature sensors, energy-efficiency improvements and sun protection, while another proposes a 10 million euro annual programme over at least four years to install air conditioning in about 20,000 homes per electoral term. The measures also include the proposed development of a mobile-accessible heat map to help residents plan routes during dangerous temperatures. Supporters said the city must act more quickly as heatwaves become more frequent and severe.
stories.headline: Barcelona considers subsidies for air conditioning and heat sensors in neighborhoods most vulnerable to extreme heat
